title: How pages render today: classes + helpers, with page.jsonl deltas on top

owner_note.text: A page is a class instance, and most pages (about 1,100) are still written as code with the little helper functions (h1(), p(), div()) inside content(){…}; nothing replaced them. A page can also be a page.jsonl log, where line 1 builds the page and each later line is one set() call, such as {"content":{"add":{"type":"part-text",…}}}, which agents append through page_set; code and those lines share one page.content list and one View, and a page can use both. Updates arrive live (the dev server tails the file and the page redraws, no polling), and any .md file is also a page under md/. The full answer, with a flow diagram and a live example of each kind: /framework/core/Page/md/doc/how-a-page-renders/
